newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai corn active, market talks on Malaysian cargo.
newsitem.headline: Thai corn active, market talks on Malaysian cargo.

text.p: Thailand's local corn market was active with feedmills on a buying spree after many decided not to import due to contraints on time and cost, trade sources said on Tuesday.
But there was a market talk that two major feedmills were seeking to divert a few cargoes of corn from Malaysia, hoping to meet an August 31 deadline.
Soymeal was also active as demand was boosted on the back of lower prices of tapioca. Tapioca and soymeal are traditional mixers for swine feed, they said.
Feedmills and end-users imported between 10,000-15,000 tonnes of of optional-origin soymeal this week, they said.
"Corn supplies were just snapped up. Although more of them are available now, it's still not enough," said a local trader.
There was no confirmation about a purchase from Malaysia.
The Thai government last month allowed the industry to import by August 31 150,000 tonnes of corn under the zero-tariff scheme to alleviate shortage caused by drought.
This was on the top of 200,000 tonnes allowed earlier this year.
But so far, only half of that amount was said to have been covered as buyers were sidelined by the tight deadline and the high premiums they had to pay in diverting cargoes in transit.
Industry sources said most of the purchases were to cover short-term positions as players were reassessing the demand outlook due to a sharp economic downturn.

"Some buyers were reluctant to buy distant contracts. Many seemed to believe that the demand for pork and poultry would either be steady or drop as consumers were hit by stagnant economy and austerity plan," said an executive at one feedmill.
"There was also a report that the market share of Thai frozen chicken exports to Japan was shrinking," he said.
The volatile baht was also a major factor that discouraged the industry from buying in a large quantities now.
The baht hit a record low of 32.900/33.100 to the dollar in the offshore market on Tuesday in line with sustained weakness of regional currencies.
Corn price was steady at 5.30 baht a kg while local soymeal was traded around 10.10-10.20 baht a kg.
